form: flat — the same form as the adjective *leisurely*
contrast: *leisurely* already ends in *-ly*, so one form serves as adjective (*a leisurely walk*) and adverb; there is no *leisurelily*. The adverb sounds a little bookish, and *at a leisurely pace* is the everyday choice: *We walked at a leisurely pace*.

senses.gloss: Slowly and in a relaxed way, without hurrying.
examples: The boat drifted *leisurely* down the river.
They strolled *leisurely* through the park after lunch.
We ate *leisurely* on the porch and watched the sun go down.

senses.gloss: In the direction of the longest side of something.
examples: Cut the zucchini in half *lengthwise*.
Fold the paper *lengthwise*, then open it again.
Lay the boards *lengthwise* across the truck bed.

senses.gloss: In a way that is less strict or severe than expected.
examples: The judge treated him *leniently* because it was his first offense.
Teachers tend to grade *leniently* in the first semester.
The dress code is applied *leniently* to new employees.

senses.gloss: Slowly and without energy or interest.
examples: He moved *lethargically* around the kitchen after the night shift.
The dog lay *lethargically* in the shade.
She shrugged *lethargically* and went back to her phone.

senses.gloss: In a crude, sexually offensive way.
examples: He winked *lewdly* at the waitress.
The comedian joked *lewdly* about his ex-wife.
Two men whistled *lewdly* as she walked past.

contrast: A false friend: Russian *либерально* suggests politics, but in everyday English *liberally* almost always means *generously, in large amounts*: *Apply sunscreen liberally*. The political idea is usually said with the adjective: *She votes liberal*, *a liberal policy*.

senses.gloss: In large amounts; generously.
examples: Apply sunscreen *liberally* before you go outside.
The chef uses garlic *liberally* in almost every dish.
The report is *liberally* sprinkled with charts and photos.

senses.gloss: Not strictly or literally; freely.
examples: The court interpreted the law *liberally*.
The movie is *liberally* adapted from the novel.

senses.gloss: As if dead; without movement, energy or feeling.
examples: His arm hung *lifelessly* over the side of the bed.
The flag drooped *lifelessly* in the still air.
She read the speech *lifelessly*, as if it were a grocery list.

form: flat — the same form as the adjective *light*
contrast: The flat adverb *light* lives in a few set phrases: *travel light*, *pack light*, *eat light*. Everywhere else use *lightly*: *She touched his arm lightly*, not *touched his arm light*. *light* in *a light bag* or *a light color* is the adjective.

senses.gloss: With little luggage or weight; without carrying or eating much.
examples: I always travel *light* — just a backpack.
Pack *light*; the airline charges for every bag.
Next time I'm going to pack *lighter*.

form: -ly from *lighthearted*; American writing often closes it up as *lightheartedly*

senses.gloss: In a cheerful, joking way; without being serious.
examples: She *light-heartedly* teased him about his new haircut.
He talked *light-heartedly* about the accident, but he was clearly shaken.
The speech began *light-heartedly* before turning serious.

position: mid or end — before a past participle (*lightly salted*)
contrast: *travel light* / *pack light* keep the flat form, but *touch lightly*, *knock lightly*, *lightly salted* take *-ly*. *take something lightly* means not seriously (*легкомысленно относиться*), and *not lightly* means after serious thought: *We didn't make this decision lightly*.

senses.gloss: Gently, with little force or weight; a little.
examples: She knocked *lightly* on the door.
*Lightly* brush the dough with melted butter.
It was snowing *lightly* when we left the house.

senses.gloss: Without being serious or thinking carefully.
examples: Don't take his threats *lightly*.
This is not a decision we made *lightly*.

senses.gloss: With less punishment or harm than expected — in *get off lightly*.
examples: He got off *lightly* with just a warning.
Compared to the other houses on our street, we got off *lightly* in the storm.

senses.gloss: Softly and without strength, firmness or energy.
examples: The flowers hung *limply* in the heat.
He shook my hand *limply* and looked away.
Her wet hair fell *limply* over her face.

senses.gloss: At a steady, proportional rate, or in a straight step-by-step order.
examples: The cost grows *linearly* with the number of users.
The story isn't told *linearly*; it jumps back and forth in time.
Prices rose almost *linearly* over the decade.

position: front or end — before its word (*linguistically diverse*)

senses.gloss: In terms of language.
examples: Queens is *linguistically* diverse — well over a hundred languages are spoken there.
*Linguistically*, Romanian is closer to Italian than to its neighbors.
Children who are *linguistically* gifted often pick up a second language fast.

senses.gloss: Without energy or interest in anything.
examples: He flipped *listlessly* through the channels.
The kids sat *listlessly* in the heat, too tired to play.
She stirred her coffee *listlessly* and stared out the window.

form: flat — the same form as the adjective *live* (rhymes with *five*)
contrast: The adverb and adjective *live* are pronounced /laɪv/, like *five*; the verb *live* (*I live in Ohio*) is /lɪv/, like *give*. *watch it live* = as it happens (*в прямом эфире*); *see a band live* = in person, not recorded (*вживую*).

senses.gloss: At the time something is actually happening, not recorded; in person.
examples: The game will be broadcast *live* on Channel 5.
I've never seen them play *live*.
We're going *live* now to our reporter in Chicago.

ru: на месте, в этом районе; местами
position: end — before a past participle (*locally grown*)

senses.gloss: In or near the area where you are or that you are talking about.
senses.ru: на месте, в этом районе, местный
examples: We buy most of our vegetables *locally*.
The restaurant only uses *locally* grown produce.
She's well known *locally* but not outside the county.

senses.gloss: In one part or area only, not everywhere.
examples: The cream should be applied *locally* to the rash.
Thunderstorms could be *locally* severe this afternoon.

senses.gloss: In a proud, superior way, or in grand, high-sounding terms.
examples: "I don't watch television," she said *loftily*.
He *loftily* dismissed his critics as amateurs.
The brochure speaks *loftily* of transforming lives but gives no details.

position: end — front as a sentence adverb (*Logically, …*)

senses.gloss: In a clear, reasoned way.
examples: Try to think *logically* about the problem.
He explained each step *logically* and slowly.
The essay isn't *logically* organized.

senses.gloss: As follows from the facts; as you would reasonably expect.
examples: *Logically*, if he left at noon, he should be here by now.
*Logically*, the next step would be to raise prices.

type: duration; also time in *no longer* and *any longer*
position: end — mid in *no longer* (*She no longer works here*)
comparison: not gradable — it is already the comparative of *long* (*much longer*)
contrast: For time use *longer*, not *more*: *Stay a little longer* (*останься подольше*), not *Stay more*. Russian *больше не* / *уже не* is *no longer* before the verb (*He no longer lives here*) or *not … any longer* at the end (*He doesn't live here any longer*), never *more not*. *no longer* sounds a little more formal than *not … anymore*.

senses.gloss: For a greater amount of time.
examples: Can you stay a little *longer*?
The drive took *longer* than we expected.
Bake it ten minutes *longer* if you like it crispy.

senses.gloss: Not now, though it was true before — in *no longer* and *not … any longer*.
examples: He *no longer* works here.
I can't wait *any longer*.

senses.gloss: In a way that shows you want something very much.
examples: The kids stared *longingly* at the ice cream truck.
She talks *longingly* about the summers she spent in Maine.
He looked *longingly* at the last slice of pizza.

position: before its word — before comparatives (*lots better*); end after a verb (*thanks lots*)
contrast: *lots* and *a lot* as adverbs are informal: *I feel lots better* / *a lot better*. In writing use *much better* or *far better*, and never *very better*. *lots of* before a noun (*lots of people*) is a quantifier, not this adverb.

senses.gloss: Much; a great deal — informal.
examples: I'm feeling *lots* better today, thanks.
Thanks *lots* for the ride!
The new apartment is *lots* bigger than our old one.

contrast: In speech *loud* also works as a flat adverb: *Can you talk louder?*, *laugh out loud*. *loudly* is the neutral form, and *more loudly* is safer in writing. *read it aloud* / *out loud* means not silently (*вслух*), not *loudly* (*громко*).

senses.gloss: With a lot of sound; also openly and forcefully.
examples: Someone was knocking *loudly* on the door.
The neighbors' dog barks *loudly* every morning at six.
Parents complained *loudly* about the new school hours.

position: mid or end — before a past participle (*lovingly restored*)

senses.gloss: With love or great care.
examples: She looked *lovingly* at her newborn son.
The old farmhouse has been *lovingly* restored.
He *lovingly* polished his car every Sunday.

senses.gloss: Faithfully, with continued support.
examples: She served the company *loyally* for thirty years.
Fans *loyally* followed the team through losing seasons.
He *loyally* defended his friend in front of everyone.

modifies: verbs of speaking, writing and thinking

senses.gloss: Clearly and in a way that is easy to understand; with a clear mind.
examples: The author explains complex ideas *lucidly*.
Even at ninety, she spoke *lucidly* about the war.
He writes *lucidly* and without jargon.

senses.gloss: To an absurd degree; in a ridiculous way.
examples: The concert tickets were *ludicrously* expensive.
The plan was *ludicrously* optimistic.
He was dressed *ludicrously* for a job interview.

position: end — before a past participle (*luridly colored*)

senses.gloss: In a shocking way that dwells on violence, sex or scandal.
examples: The tabloids *luridly* described every detail of the murder.
The book *luridly* recounts the rock star's years of drug abuse.

senses.gloss: In very bright, harsh colors.
examples: The sky glowed *luridly* orange over the burning hills.
The motel sign flashed *luridly* in the rain.

contrast: Not the same as *lustily*, which means loudly and with energy: *The crowd sang lustily* has nothing to do with desire.

senses.gloss: With strong sexual desire.
examples: He stared *lustfully* at the woman across the bar.
The two main characters glance *lustfully* at each other for three hundred pages.
The ad shows a man gazing *lustfully* at a double cheeseburger.

contrast: A trap: *lustily* has nothing to do with desire. It means loudly and with energy (*sing lustily*, *cheer lustily*). The sexual meaning is *lustfully*.

senses.gloss: Loudly and with a lot of energy and enthusiasm.
examples: The crowd sang the national anthem *lustily*.
The baby cried *lustily* until someone picked her up.
Fans booed *lustily* when the referee made the call.

position: end — before a past participle (*luxuriously furnished*)

senses.gloss: In a rich, expensive and comfortable way; with great comfort or pleasure.
examples: The hotel rooms are *luxuriously* furnished.
The cat stretched *luxuriously* in the sun.
They lived *luxuriously* on his salary alone.

position: end — front as a viewpoint adverb (*Lyrically, …*)

senses.gloss: In a beautiful, emotional way, like poetry.
examples: She writes *lyrically* about her childhood in rural Georgia.
The film is *lyrically* shot, with long, quiet scenes of the prairie.

senses.gloss: In terms of the words of a song.
examples: *Lyrically*, the new album is much darker than their last one.
The song is catchy but *lyrically* pretty weak.

position: end — before its word in *madly in love*
modifies: verbs; *in love* and a few adjectives
contrast: In American English *mad* usually means *angry* (*She's mad at me*), but *madly* almost never means *angrily*: it means wildly or extremely. *He was madly waving* = frantically, not angrily.

senses.gloss: In a wild, frantic way.
examples: She was typing *madly* to finish before the deadline.
The dog barked *madly* at the mail carrier.
Fans waved *madly* as the band came on stage.

senses.gloss: Extremely — mostly in *madly in love*.
examples: They're *madly* in love.
He was *madly* jealous of his older brother.

senses.gloss: As if by magic; in a wonderful, unexplained way.
examples: The problem isn't going to *magically* disappear.
The doors *magically* opened as we walked up.
The fresh snow made the town look *magically* quiet.

senses.gloss: Generously and kindly, especially toward a rival or someone who has lost.
examples: The winner *magnanimously* praised her opponent.
He *magnanimously* offered to split the prize money.
The company acted *magnanimously* toward the workers it laid off.

position: end — before a past participle (*magnetically attached*)

senses.gloss: By means of a magnet or magnetism.
examples: The case attaches *magnetically* to the back of the phone.
Old cassette tapes stored music *magnetically*.
The train is *magnetically* lifted above the track.

position: end — before a past participle (*magnificently restored*)

senses.gloss: Extremely well; in a very impressive or beautiful way.
examples: The orchestra played *magnificently*.
The old theater has been *magnificently* restored.
She handled the crisis *magnificently*.

senses.gloss: In a grand, impressive and beautiful way.
examples: An eagle soared *majestically* over the canyon.
The mountains rise *majestically* above the lake.
The old ship sailed *majestically* into the harbor.

senses.gloss: In a way that shows a wish to harm others.
examples: The villain grinned *malevolently* at the camera.
The cat stared *malevolently* at the new puppy.
He smiled *malevolently* as he signed the eviction notice.

senses.gloss: On purpose, with the intention of hurting someone or causing damage.
examples: Someone *maliciously* deleted all the files on the server.
She was accused of *maliciously* spreading rumors about a coworker.
The program was *maliciously* designed to steal passwords.

senses.gloss: Bravely and with great effort, especially when you are likely to fail.
examples: He tried *manfully* to hold back his tears.
The goalie battled *manfully*, but the team still lost 5-1.
Our old car struggled *manfully* up the mountain road.

senses.gloss: In a wild, crazy or obsessive way.
examples: The villain laughed *maniacally*.
He cleaned the house *maniacally* before his parents arrived.
She worked *maniacally* through the night to finish the paper.

position: before its word — also mid (*has manifestly failed*)

senses.gloss: Clearly and obviously — formal.
examples: The decision was *manifestly* unfair.
That claim is *manifestly* untrue.
The policy has *manifestly* failed.

form: compound — also written *man to man* after a verb; always hyphenated before a noun (*a man-to-man talk*)
contrast: In basketball and soccer, *man-to-man defense* is an adjective use: each player guards one opponent (*персональная опека*).

senses.gloss: Openly and honestly, as one man to another.
examples: Son, it's time we talked *man-to-man*.
He went to see his boss and spoke to him *man-to-man*.
Let's settle this *man-to-man*, without the lawyers.

senses.gloss: By hand or by a person, not automatically.
examples: You'll have to enter the data *manually*.
The gate can be opened *manually* if the power goes out.
I *manually* updated the app because it wouldn't update on its own.

position: before its word — before adjectives and comparatives; also end (*improved markedly*)
modifies: adjectives, comparatives and verbs of change
contrast: *marked* has one syllable (/mɑːrkt/), but *markedly* has three: MAHR-kid-lee, never *markt-lee*.

senses.gloss: Clearly and noticeably; to a large degree.
examples: Her English has improved *markedly* this year.
The two plans are *markedly* different.
Crime is *markedly* lower than it was a decade ago.

senses.gloss: Extremely well; wonderfully.
examples: The kids behaved *marvelously* at the wedding.
Everything worked out *marvelously* in the end.
The fish was *marvelously* fresh.

position: before its word — also end (*grew massively*)
contrast: Russian *массово* (by many people at once, on a mass scale) is not usually *massively*. *massively* means hugely, to a very great degree: *massively popular*, *massively over budget*. For *массово* try *in large numbers* or *en masse*: *People left the city in large numbers*.

senses.gloss: Very much; to a very great degree.
examples: The show was *massively* popular with teenagers.
The project went *massively* over budget.
Rents have gone up *massively* since 2020.

position: mid or end — before a past participle (*masterfully edited*)

senses.gloss: With great skill.
examples: She *masterfully* handled the tough questions from reporters.
The film is *masterfully* edited.
He played the final piece *masterfully*.

position: before its word — also end (*better off materially*)
contrast: Russian *материально* is about money (*материально обеспечен*). English *materially* can mean that, but in formal and legal writing it usually means *significantly*: *The facts have not materially changed*. For money in everyday speech, *financially* is more natural.

senses.gloss: Significantly; in an important way — formal.
examples: The new evidence did not *materially* change the verdict.
The two contracts are not *materially* different.
His health has *materially* improved since the surgery.

senses.gloss: In terms of money and possessions.
examples: They were *materially* comfortable but deeply unhappy.
The family is better off *materially* than it was ten years ago.

position: front or end — before its word (*mathematically impossible*)

senses.gloss: In terms of numbers or mathematics; using mathematics.
examples: It's *mathematically* impossible for us to make the playoffs now.
*Mathematically*, the odds of winning are one in 300 million.
She proved the theory *mathematically*.

senses.gloss: In a sensible, adult way.
examples: She handled the breakup very *maturely*.
I expect you to behave *maturely* on the field trip.
He reacted *maturely* for a fourteen-year-old.

contrast: Russian *максимально* is everyday (*максимально быстро*), but English *maximally* is formal or technical. In speech say *as fast as possible*, not *maximally fast*.

senses.gloss: To the greatest possible degree.
examples: The software is designed to be *maximally* efficient.
The layout is *maximally* simple: one button, one screen.
The drug works best when the muscle is *maximally* relaxed.

position: mid or end — before a past participle (*meagerly paid*)

senses.gloss: In an amount that is too small; poorly.
examples: Teachers there are *meagerly* paid.
The museum is *meagerly* funded and relies on volunteers.
The shelves were *meagerly* stocked after the storm.

position: end — mid before a verb (*hasn't meaningfully changed*)

senses.gloss: In a way that shows a hidden meaning without saying it.
examples: She looked *meaningfully* at the clock.
He coughed *meaningfully* and nodded toward the door.

senses.gloss: In a real, significant or useful way.
examples: The new law hasn't *meaningfully* reduced crime.
We want every student to take part *meaningfully* in class.

position: front — usually as *in the meantime*; also end
form: compound — *mean* (middle) + *time*; also a noun in *in the meantime*
contrast: Alone, *Meantime, …* is less common than *meanwhile* or the noun phrase *in the meantime*. All three mean *тем временем*, but *in the meantime* is the usual choice for *пока что*, until something happens: *The doctor will see you soon. In the meantime, fill out this form*.

senses.gloss: In the time between two events; until something expected happens.
examples: Dinner will be ready at seven. *Meantime*, help yourself to some snacks.
The repairs will take a week. *Meantime*, use the back door.
The new manager starts in May; *meantime*, Sarah is running the office.

position: before its word — also end (*improved measurably*)
modifies: adjectives, comparatives and verbs of change

senses.gloss: By an amount large enough to notice or measure.
examples: The new filters made the water *measurably* cleaner.
Test scores improved *measurably* after the program started.
She's been *measurably* happier since she changed jobs.

senses.gloss: By machine, or in terms of how machines and engines work.
examples: The car is *mechanically* sound, but the paint is peeling.
The windows are opened and closed *mechanically*.
My brother has always been *mechanically* minded.

senses.gloss: Without thinking or feeling, like a machine.
examples: She nodded *mechanically*, not really listening.
He signed the papers *mechanically*, one after another.

senses.gloss: As a medicine; for treating illness.
examples: The plant has been used *medicinally* for centuries.
In many states, marijuana can be used *medicinally* with a doctor's note.
He claims he only drinks whiskey *medicinally*.

senses.gloss: Slowly and quietly, as if deep in thought.
examples: He chewed his sandwich *meditatively* and said nothing.
She stared *meditatively* at the lake.
Grandpa rubbed his chin *meditatively* before he answered.

senses.gloss: Quietly and obediently, without arguing.
examples: He *meekly* apologized and sat back down.
The kids followed the teacher *meekly* back inside.
She accepted the decision *meekly*, without a word.

senses.gloss: In an exaggerated, overly emotional way.
examples: "My life is over," she sighed *melodramatically*.
He clutched his chest *melodramatically* when he saw the bill.
The teenager *melodramatically* slammed her bedroom door.

position: end — front as *most memorably*; mid before a verb

senses.gloss: In a way that is easy to remember or worth remembering.
examples: She once *memorably* compared Congress to a kindergarten class.
The concert ended *memorably*, with the whole crowd singing along.
We saw a lot on the trip, but *most memorably* a bear on the trail.

senses.gloss: In a threatening way.
examples: The dog growled *menacingly* at the stranger.
Dark clouds gathered *menacingly* over the lake.
He stepped *menacingly* toward me.

position: front — also mid, and before its word in *mercifully short*

senses.gloss: Fortunately; to everyone's relief.
examples: The speeches were *mercifully* short.
*Mercifully*, nobody was hurt.
The rain *mercifully* stopped before the game started.

senses.gloss: With mercy; kindly, instead of harshly.
examples: The judge acted *mercifully* toward the young offender.
The general treated the prisoners *mercifully*.

senses.gloss: Cruelly and without stopping; without mercy.
examples: The other kids teased him *mercilessly*.
The sun beat down *mercilessly* on the players.
Critics *mercilessly* attacked the film.

senses.gloss: In a happy, cheerful way; also carelessly, without noticing a problem.
examples: The children sang *merrily* around the campfire.
A fire crackled *merrily* in the fireplace.
He went on *merrily* spending money he didn't have.

position: end — before a past participle (*messily tied*)

senses.gloss: In an untidy or dirty way; also in a complicated, unpleasant way.
examples: The toddler ate his spaghetti *messily*.
Her hair was *messily* pulled back into a bun.
The marriage ended *messily*, with lawyers on both sides.

senses.gloss: In terms of metabolism, the way the body turns food into energy.
examples: Muscle is more *metabolically* active than fat.
Some people are overweight but *metabolically* healthy.
*Metabolically*, a hummingbird burns energy at an amazing rate.

modifies: verbs of speaking and understanding; whole clauses

senses.gloss: Not literally; using an image or comparison to express an idea.
examples: I didn't mean it literally — I was speaking *metaphorically*.
*Metaphorically* speaking, we're all in the same boat.
The bridge in the novel can be read *metaphorically* as a symbol of hope.

senses.gloss: Carefully and in a fixed order, one step at a time.
examples: The detective *methodically* searched every room.
She worked *methodically* through the list.
He *methodically* folded each shirt and put it in the suitcase.

position: mid or end — before a past participle (*meticulously researched*)

senses.gloss: With very great care and attention to every detail.
examples: The book is *meticulously* researched.
She *meticulously* planned every detail of the wedding.
He cleans his camera lenses *meticulously*.

position: before its word — end for the microscope sense

senses.gloss: Extremely — about something very small.
examples: The print on the label was *microscopically* small.
Her chances of winning were *microscopically* low.

senses.gloss: With or under a microscope.
examples: The samples were examined *microscopically*.
The bacteria can only be seen *microscopically*.

form: compound — *mid-* + *week*; also an adjective (*a midweek flight*)

senses.gloss: In the middle of the week, around Tuesday to Thursday.
examples: Flights are usually cheaper if you fly *midweek*.
The storm should reach the East Coast *midweek*.
Let's meet *midweek* to check on the project.

position: end — mid before a past participle (*mightily impressed*)

senses.gloss: With great effort or force.
examples: The team struggled *mightily* in the second half.
She fought *mightily* to keep the store open.

senses.gloss: Very; greatly.
examples: We were all *mightily* impressed.
The news pleased him *mightily*.

form: flat — the same form as the adjective *mighty*
contrast: *mighty* as an intensifier (*mighty kind*, *mighty cold*) is informal, folksy American speech and can sound old-fashioned or rural; in writing use *very*. The adjective means powerful: *a mighty river*, *a mighty army*.

senses.gloss: Very — informal.
examples: That's *mighty* kind of you.
It's getting *mighty* cold out there.
You look *mighty* pleased with yourself.

position: front or end — before its word (*militarily weak*)
form: -ly from *military*; the stress moves to the third syllable (MIL-i-ter-ee → mil-i-TER-uh-lee)

senses.gloss: In terms of armed forces, or by using them.
examples: The country is *militarily* weak but economically strong.
The president refused to intervene *militarily*.
*Militarily*, the operation was a success.

senses.gloss: With careful attention to what you are doing or feeling right now.
examples: Try to eat *mindfully*, without your phone on the table.
She breathed slowly and *mindfully* before the interview.
We're trying to spend our money *mindfully* this year.

senses.gloss: Without thinking or paying attention; for no good reason.
examples: I spent the evening *mindlessly* scrolling through my phone.
He *mindlessly* followed the crowd.
The workers repeated the same task *mindlessly* for hours.

senses.gloss: To a very small degree; as little as possible.
examples: The surgery is *minimally* invasive.
Our town was only *minimally* affected by the storm.
The room was *minimally* furnished — just a bed and a chair.

position: end — before a past participle (*minutely planned*)
contrast: *minutely* comes from the adjective *minute* (/maɪˈnuːt/, tiny), not the noun *minute* (/ˈmɪnɪt/). It means in tiny detail or by a tiny amount, never *every minute*; for that say *every minute* or *by the minute*.

senses.gloss: In very close detail; also by a very small amount.
examples: The experts examined the painting *minutely*.
Every step of the trip was *minutely* planned.
The numbers changed only *minutely* from last year.

senses.gloss: Surprisingly and luckily, as if by a miracle.
examples: *Miraculously*, no one was injured in the crash.
The old dog *miraculously* survived three days in the snow.
Her cancer *miraculously* went into remission.

contrast: Stress the first syllable, and there is no extra *-ee-*: MIS-chi-vuhs-lee, not *mis-CHEE-vee-uhs-lee*. The spelling has no *i* after *v*: *mischievous*, not *mischievious*.

senses.gloss: In a playful way that suggests harmless trouble.
examples: The boy grinned *mischievously* and ran off.
Her eyes sparkled *mischievously*.
"Guess what I did," she whispered *mischievously*.

senses.gloss: In a very unhappy way.
examples: He sat *miserably* in the rain, waiting for the bus.
"I lost my wallet," she said *miserably*.

senses.gloss: Very badly — mostly in *fail miserably*.
examples: The plan failed *miserably*.
Our team played *miserably* in the second half.

position: mid — before a verb or past participle; also before its word (*misleadingly simple*)

senses.gloss: In a way that gives a wrong idea.
examples: The juice was *misleadingly* labeled as all natural.
The ad *misleadingly* suggests that the phone is waterproof.
The recipe's name is *misleadingly* simple.

senses.gloss: Wrongly; because of a mistake.
examples: Many people *mistakenly* believe that bats are blind.
The package was *mistakenly* delivered to our neighbor.
He was *mistakenly* identified as the driver.

senses.gloss: In a way that makes fun of someone.
examples: "Oh, poor baby," he said *mockingly*.
She bowed *mockingly* to the audience.
The other players clapped *mockingly* when he finally caught the ball.

position: end — before its word in *modestly priced*

senses.gloss: Without boasting; also in a plain way that is not showy.
examples: "It was nothing," he said *modestly*.
She dresses *modestly* for work.
They live *modestly* in a small house outside town.

senses.gloss: By a small amount; not too much.
examples: The restaurant is *modestly* priced.
Sales rose *modestly* last quarter.
